title: Releasing Typemaid on NPM Turning your mermaid diagrams into AI workflows
text: I've been privately building a TypeScript SDK called TypeMaid and using it for my own projects over the past month. text:
I used to use Fabricate a long time ago, its strace based build was a great idea and I always wanted something that could track dependencies so I didn't have to. KIZZ is that, it tracks your dependencies, and also the order of the build.  It won't rebuild if nothing changes, and can be scripted with literal markdown files with starlark build steps.  I call this building in positive space, not negative space. Linux only because Win/Mac make doing this very very hard on those platforms.
It can also be used to work out dependencies for another build tool, so you're not guessing anymore.
